title: Brazil's Monkeys Have Used Stone Tools for 3,000 Years
subject: capuchin monkey

scenes.text: There's a Stone Age in Brazil that never ended.
The workers are wild capuchin monkeys, and they use rocks as hammers.
Archaeologists dug up 122 of their stone tools in Serra da Capivara National Park.
Radiocarbon dating put the oldest at around 3,000 years. That's roughly 450 monkey generations.
And the tools changed. Small stones for soft seeds back then. Bigger stones for hard nuts about 300 years ago.
Today they crack cashews with a similar rock. Their Stone Age never stopped.

description:
There's a Stone Age in Brazil that never ended, and the workers are wild capuchin monkeys.
Archaeologists recovered 122 stone tools from four layers at a site in Serra da Capivara National Park. Radiocarbon dating shows capuchins have used stones for around 3,000 years, and the tools changed over time, from small pounders for soft seeds to bigger stones for hard nuts.
Which animal would you most like to watch use a tool?
first_comment: Before this study, only humans and our ancestors had a known archaeological record of tool use in primates. Do you think other animals have a hidden Stone Age too?
